articles.title: State by state Social Security cuts: Which states could lose the most and how much?
articles.standfirst: Retirees aren't facing state-imposed reductions, but projected federal funding problems could cut monthly benefits nationwide if Congress doesn't act
articles.summary: Retirees aren't facing state-imposed reductions, but projected federal funding problems could cut monthly benefits nationwide if Congress doesn't act
articles.body:
Social Security recipients across the United States could face substantial benefit reductions by 2032 if lawmakers fail to address the program's worsening finances, with some retirees potentially losing more than $500 every month.

The cuts wouldn't be imposed individually by state governments. Instead, they would result from the projected insolvency of Social Security's retirement trust fund , which could leave the program able to pay only around 76% of scheduled benefits.

The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget estimates that this would translate into an approximately 24% across-the-board reduction, with the average retiree losing about $500 per month.

"No state would be spared from the potentially devastating effects of insolvency," the group warned.

Which states could see the biggest Social Security cuts?

The dollar impact would vary because average Social Security payments differ across the country.

Connecticut retirees face the largest projected average loss at $556 per month, followed by New Jersey and New Hampshire at roughly $554 and $553 respectively.

Delaware could lose $549, Maryland $541, Washington $531, Minnesota $530, Massachusetts $527, Michigan and Utah $523, Virginia $522, Kansas $520, Pennsylvania and Rhode Island $519, and Vermont $516.

Those figures don't mean retirees in those states are being specifically targeted. Higher average lifetime earnings generally produce larger Social Security checks, so a 24% reduction naturally creates a larger dollar loss.

Cuts aren't guaranteed to happen

Retirees in lower benefit states would still suffer significant reductions. Mississippi has the smallest projected average cut at $459 per month, followed by Louisiana at $460 and Arkansas at $469.

The crucial point is that none of these reductions is currently scheduled as a deliberate benefit cut.

They represent what could happen automatically if the retirement trust fund becomes depleted and Congress doesn't change taxes, benefits or other parts of the program beforehand.

Social Security would also continue paying benefits after insolvency because payroll taxes would still provide revenue. Checks wouldn't disappear completely, but scheduled payments couldn't be made in full.

Lawmakers therefore still have several years to intervene.

Possible solutions include increasing Social Security payroll tax revenue, changing retirement rules or modifying benefits, although each option carries political and financial tradeoffs.

Without action, however, retirees in every state could eventually see noticeably smaller monthly checks, with the highest average losses approaching $560.

articles.title: FAFSA application 2026: How to apply and what are the requirements for student loans?
articles.standfirst: Students seeking federal financial aid need to complete the FAFSA, provide income information and meet basic eligibility rules
articles.summary: Students seeking federal financial aid need to complete the FAFSA, provide income information and meet basic eligibility rules
articles.body:
Students planning to attend college during the 2026 to 2027 academic year will usually need to complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid , better known as the FAFSA , before they can qualify for federal student loans and other forms of financial assistance.

The FAFSA is used to determine eligibility for federal grants, work-study programs and loans, while many states and colleges also rely on the application when awarding their own aid.

Students don't pay to submit the FAFSA, and the form can be completed online through the Federal Student Aid website.

How do you apply for FAFSA in 2026?

Applicants first need to create a StudentAid.gov account , which is also known as an FSA ID.

Dependent students will generally need at least one parent or other contributor to create their own account as well. Each contributor must provide the required information and consent to the transfer of federal tax data when applicable.

Students are asked for details including their Social Security number, citizenship status, household information, finances and the schools they want to receive their FAFSA information.

After the required sections are completed and signed, the form can be submitted electronically. Applicants should then review their FAFSA Submission Summary and correct any errors if necessary.

What are the requirements for federal student loans?

Completing the FAFSA doesn't automatically guarantee a loan , but it is generally required before federal aid can be offered.

Applicants must meet basic federal eligibility requirements, including being a U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen, having a valid Social Security number in most cases and being enrolled or accepted into an eligible degree or certificate program.

Students also need to maintain satisfactory academic progress once they are in school.

Federal Direct Loans are usually available without a credit check for undergraduate students. Graduate PLUS and Parent PLUS loans operate differently and can involve a review of adverse credit history.

Schools use FAFSA information to create individual financial aid offers, meaning the amount available can vary significantly from one student to another.

Students should also pay close attention to deadlines .

The federal FAFSA deadline is only one part of the process, as states and individual colleges can set much earlier priority dates for grants and other limited aid.

Submitting the form as early as possible can therefore improve a student's chances of accessing programs that run out of funding before the federal deadline arrives.

articles.title: Chapter 31 VA Benefits: What does this chapter cover and how much will you get monthly for it?
articles.standfirst: Veterans with service-connected disabilities may qualify for career support, education, training and a monthly subsistence allowance
articles.summary: Veterans with service-connected disabilities may qualify for career support, education, training and a monthly subsistence allowance
articles.body:
Chapter 31 VA benefits can provide much more than help paying for school, with eligible veterans able to receive career counseling, job training and financial support while preparing for suitable employment.

Officially called Veteran Readiness and Employment , or VR&E, the program is designed for veterans and service members whose service-connected disabilities limit their ability to work or prevent them from working.

Depending on the individual rehabilitation plan, Chapter 31 can cover college, vocational or technical training, apprenticeships, on-the-job training, and other employment services. Support can also include resume preparation, job placement assistance, counseling and help with workplace accommodations.

Some participants may also qualify for services intended to help them live more independently when employment isn't currently possible.

How much does Chapter 31 pay each month?

There isn't one universal monthly payment because the standard Chapter 31 subsistence allowance depends on training type, attendance level and the number of dependents.

Under the fiscal year 2026 rates effective October 1, 2025, a veteran in full-time institutional training receives $812.84 per month with no dependents.

That rises to $1,008.24 with one dependent and $1,188.15 with two dependents. An additional $86.58 is added for each further dependent.

Three-quarter-time institutional training pays $610.76 with no dependents, while half-time training pays $408.66.

The VA lists a maximum Chapter 31 monthly subsistence allowance of $3,439.23, although that unusually high ceiling assumes a veteran with a very large number of eligible dependents and shouldn't be treated as a typical payment.

Who qualifies for Chapter 31 benefits?

Veterans can generally apply if they didn't receive a dishonorable discharge and have a VA service-connected disability rating of at least 10%.

Applying doesn't automatically guarantee entitlement. A VA Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor evaluates the veteran's circumstances and determines whether VR&E services are appropriate.

Veterans who are also eligible for the Post-9/11 GI Bill may have another valuable option.

Someone with at least one day of remaining Chapter 33 entitlement who is still within their GI Bill eligibility period can elect the Post-9/11 GI Bill subsistence rate instead of the standard Chapter 31 allowance.

The VA says that rate is higher in most cases, so eligible participants should compare both options with their counselor before choosing how they'll be paid.

articles.title: Max Social Security Tax 2026: How is Social Security going to be taxed?
articles.standfirst: The 2026 rules mean higher earners will face a larger payroll-tax bill, while retirees may also owe federal income tax on part of their benefits
articles.summary: The 2026 rules mean higher earners will face a larger payroll-tax bill, while retirees may also owe federal income tax on part of their benefits
articles.body:
S ocial Security taxation can be confusing because there are two different taxes that often get discussed under the same name.

Workers pay Social Security payroll taxes on their earnings, while some retirees must pay federal income tax on part of the Social Security benefits they receive.

For 2026, the maximum amount of earnings subject to the Social Security payroll tax has increased significantly. The Social Security Administration (SSA) says the taxable maximum, also known as the contribution and benefit base, is $184,500, compared with $176,100 in 2025.

That means workers earning more than $184,500 do not pay the 6.2% employee Social Security tax on wages above that threshold. Their employers also pay 6.2% on taxable wages, while self-employed workers generally pay the combined 12.4% rate themselves, subject to the applicable rules.

For an employee who earns at least $184,500 in 2026, the maximum employee Social Security tax is therefore $11,439. The employer would contribute another $11,439.

The increase in the wage base means high earners can expect more Social Security tax to be withheld during the year before they reach the new ceiling.

How much of your Social Security benefits can be taxed?

The payroll tax is only one side of the story. Once you begin receiving Social Security , the federal government can potentially tax part of those benefits depending on your overall income.

The IRS uses a calculation known as combined income, which generally includes adjusted gross income, tax-exempt interest and half of your Social Security benefits.

For single filers, Social Security benefits can become partially taxable once combined income exceeds $25,000. Between $25,000 and $34,000, up to 50% of benefits may be taxable. Above $34,000, as much as 85% of benefits can be included in taxable income.

For married couples filing jointly, the corresponding thresholds are $32,000 and $44,000. Once combined income exceeds $44,000, up to 85% of Social Security benefits can be taxable.

Importantly, 85% taxable does not mean an 85% tax rate. It means that up to 85% of the benefit can be included in taxable income and then taxed according to the person's applicable federal income-tax rate.

The thresholds have remained unchanged for decades, which means more retirees can potentially find themselves paying federal income tax on their benefits as wages, pensions and other retirement income increase.

What does the $184,500 limit mean for your future benefits?

The taxable maximum also matters when calculating future Social Security benefits. The SSA says earnings above the annual limit aren't counted when determining benefits.

Consequently, someone earning $300,000 does not receive additional Social Security credit for the portion of their salary above $184,500 in 2026. The same principle applies when determining the amount of earnings subject to Social Security taxation.

The maximum benefit is also tied to factors including earnings history and the age at which someone claims benefits. For 2026, the SSA lists the maximum monthly retirement benefit for someone retiring at full retirement age at $4,152.

Another important distinction is Medicare. Unlike Social Security , Medicare's Hospital Insurance payroll tax has no earnings ceiling, so high-income workers continue paying the basic Medicare tax on all covered wages. Higher earners can also face an additional Medicare tax.

The 2026 Social Security changes therefore affect both sides of retirement planning: workers earning above the wage base will see a higher maximum payroll-tax contribution, while retirees need to consider whether other income could make part of their Social Security benefits taxable.

For an individual estimate, the SSA's online tools can provide a personalized projection based on a worker's earnings record and expected claiming age.

articles.title: How to know if you qualify for the $4,427 EITC payment and when will you get it?
articles.standfirst: The 2026 Earned Income Tax Credit could provide thousands of dollars to eligible workers and families
articles.summary: The 2026 Earned Income Tax Credit could provide thousands of dollars to eligible workers and families
articles.body:
The Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) can be worth thousands of dollars to eligible low- and moderate-income workers, but the widely cited $4,427 figure is a maximum, not a guaranteed payment.

For tax year 2026, a taxpayer with one qualifying child can receive up to $4,427, while the maximum rises to $7,316 for two qualifying children and $8,231 for three or more. Workers without qualifying children can receive a maximum of $664.

That distinction is important because the EITC is calculated according to several factors, including earned income, adjusted gross income, filing status and the number of qualifying children.

The credit generally increases as earnings rise, reaches a maximum and then gradually phases out as income moves above the applicable threshold.

The EITC is also refundable, meaning an eligible taxpayer can receive money even if the credit is larger than their federal income-tax liability.

The Tax Policy Center explains that refundable credits can result in the excess being paid to the taxpayer rather than simply reducing a tax bill to zero.

For 2026, the maximum $4,427 credit applies to taxpayers with one qualifying child. For taxpayers filing under statuses other than married filing jointly, the credit begins phasing out once earned income or adjusted gross income reaches $23,890 and disappears at $51,593.

For married couples filing jointly, the corresponding phase-out range is $31,160 to $58,863.

Who can qualify for the $4,427 EITC?

There are several basic requirements that workers must satisfy before they can claim the credit.

The IRS says taxpayers generally need earned income, must have a valid Social Security number and must be a U.S. citizen or resident alien for the entire year. They also cannot file Form 2555 for foreign earned income.

The definition of earned income generally covers money received from working, including wages, salaries, tips and certain self-employment income. Simply having a low income does not automatically qualify someone for the EITC .

For taxpayers claiming children, the child must meet specific requirements concerning age, relationship, residency and Social Security number.

A qualifying child generally must have lived with the taxpayer in the United States for more than half of the year, subject to applicable exceptions.

There are also restrictions on investment income. For tax year 2026, the IRS says the EITC is unavailable when certain investment income exceeds $12,200.

The EITC is not exclusively for parents. A worker without a qualifying child may also qualify, although additional age and residency requirements apply. In general, childless claimants must be at least 25 but under 65.

When will you receive the money?

The timing depends on which tax year is being discussed. The $4,427 maximum applies to tax year 2026, meaning taxpayers generally will claim it when they file their 2026 federal income-tax returns in 2027.

It is therefore misleading to describe every $4,427 EITC reference as an immediate payment being sent in 2026.

If you are instead filing a 2025 tax return during 2026, the maximum EITC with one qualifying child is $4,328, rather than $4,427.

Taxpayers claiming the EITC should also be aware that federal law requires the IRS to hold refunds involving the EITC or Additional Child Tax Credit until at least mid-February.

The IRS cannot issue those refunds before the statutory waiting period ends, even when the return is filed early.

The safest way to determine whether you qualify is to use the IRS's EITC Assistant and enter information for the correct tax year.

The precise credit depends on individual circumstances, so the $4,427 headline figure should be viewed as the upper limit for a specific qualifying group rather than a flat payment available to everyone.

articles.summary: From new-member Shop Cards to a current SameDay discount, here are the Costco savings worth checking before you shop
articles.body:
Costco shoppers looking for a discount in August 2026 have several offers to consider, although the retailer's promotions can change quickly.

While third-party coupon websites list numerous Costco codes, the most reliable savings tend to come from Costco's own membership promotions and limited-time sales.

As of August 20, several Costco offers are worth knowing about. Groupon's current Costco coupon page lists 14 offers, including a promotion giving new members a Digital Costco Shop Card worth up to $40.

CouponFollow is also listing the same new-member promotion, along with other advertised discounts and product-specific deals.

One important point for shoppers: not every offer described as a Costco "promo code" is a universal discount code that can be applied to any Costco.com order. Some are membership incentives, while others apply only to selected products or SameDay delivery purchases.

The most useful offers therefore depend on what you are buying and whether you already have a Costco membership.

articles.title: VA Education Benefits: What are the current programs you can apply to get benefits?
articles.standfirst: From the Post-9/11 GI Bill to career training and scholarships, veterans and eligible family members have several routes to education assistance
articles.summary: From the Post-9/11 GI Bill to career training and scholarships, veterans and eligible family members have several routes to education assistance
articles.body:
Veterans, service members and qualifying family members have access to several Department of Veterans Affairs education programs that can help cover the cost of college, vocational training, apprenticeships and other career preparation.

The Post-9/11 GI Bill, Montgomery GI Bill and Montgomery GI Bill Selected Reserve remain among the principal programs available, but they are not the only options.

The VA also administers programs aimed at survivors and dependents, STEM students and veterans pursuing technology-focused training.

The right program depends heavily on a person's military history, discharge status, type of education or training and, in some cases, their relationship to a veteran or service member.

Which VA education programs are available?

The Post-9/11 GI Bill, or Chapter 33, is one of the most comprehensive options. Generally, veterans may qualify if they served at least 90 days on active duty after September 10, 2001, although there are additional eligibility routes.

The program can help with tuition and fees, housing, books and supplies, as well as certain tests, tutoring, work-study and career training.

For the 2026-27 academic year, VA benefit rates were updated for payments beginning August 1, 2026. A veteran's percentage of eligibility depends partly on qualifying service.

Those who completed at least 36 months of active-duty service, for example, can qualify for the full 100% benefit under the standard Post-9/11 eligibility rules.

The Montgomery GI Bill Active Duty (MGIB-AD), Chapter 30, is another option. It is generally available to veterans who completed at least two years of active-duty service and satisfy other requirements, including qualifying discharge and education requirements.

There is also the Montgomery GI Bill Selected Reserve, Chapter 1606, designed for qualifying members of the Selected Reserve. Depending on eligibility, the benefit can help pay for approved education and training.

For veterans pursuing certain science, technology, engineering or mathematics fields, the Edith Nourse Rogers STEM Scholarship can provide additional assistance after qualifying Post-9/11 GI Bill entitlement has been exhausted. The VA lists current STEM Scholarship rates alongside its other education programs.

Another newer option is VET TEC 2.0, or Veteran Employment Through Technology Education Courses.

The program provides assistance for eligible veterans participating in approved high-tech education and training, including support for certain training and housing costs. The VA began accepting applications for VET TEC 2.0 in 2026.

Benefits can also extend to families

VA education assistance is not limited to veterans themselves. Eligible spouses and children can potentially receive Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA), also known as Chapter 35, when the veteran or service member meets specific conditions, including death, missing status or permanent and total service-connected disability.

The Fry Scholarship is another important program for certain children and surviving spouses of service members who died on or after September 11, 2001. It can provide money for tuition, housing, books and supplies.

Eligible service members can also potentially transfer unused Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits to a spouse or child, although the Department of Defense must approve the transfer.

There have also been important developments concerning veterans with multiple qualifying periods of service.

Following recent court decisions, some veterans who qualify for both the Post-9/11 GI Bill and MGIB-AD may now be eligible for up to 48 months of combined entitlement, rather than the traditional 36-month limit. VA says it is automatically reviewing eligibility under the relevant rulings.

How to apply for VA education benefits

Veterans and service members can apply online through the VA . For first-time applicants, VA Form 22-1990 can be used for the Post-9/11 GI Bill, MGIB-AD and MGIB-SR. Applicants should have their Social Security number, direct-deposit information and military and education history available.

Before choosing a program, applicants should use the VA's GI Bill Comparison Tool and check their eligibility.

The value of benefits can differ substantially between programs, so selecting the right benefit before beginning a course or training program can make a significant difference to the financial assistance available.

articles.title: Two university cyclists killed and more injured after tragic accident in Tennessee
articles.standfirst: Milligan University is mourning two students after a vehicle struck its cycling team during a training ride in Carter County
articles.summary: Milligan University is mourning two students after a vehicle struck its cycling team during a training ride in Carter County
articles.body:
What began as a regular training session for Milligan University's cycling team ended with two students dead and seven others injured after a vehicle collided with the group in northeastern Tennessee .

The crash happened Wednesday morning in the Hampton area of Carter County, roughly 11 miles from Milligan's campus. Eleven student cyclists were riding together when they were struck on the highway, according to university and state officials.

Milligan later identified the two students who died as sophomores Haylan Engdahl , from Winthrop Harbor, Illinois, and Brayden Rogers , from Huntsville, Alabama . Their deaths have left the university community and the wider collegiate cycling world facing a devastating loss.

Seven other members of the group were taken to Johnson City Medical Center. Four were reported to be in critical condition, two were stable and another had been discharged from the hospital.

Emergency responders were sent to the scene after the collision, with medical helicopters involved in transporting some of the injured riders. The extent of the destruction underscored the severity of the crash, with witnesses describing bicycles left badly damaged at the scene.

The driver involved was identified as 69-year-old John Benfield of Newland, North Carolina. Carter County District Attorney General Steven Finney said Benfield faces two counts of vehicular homicide by recklessness and five counts of aggravated assault by vehicle by recklessness. Authorities have indicated that additional charges could still be considered.

Authorities are still working to establish what happened

Investigators have not yet provided a complete explanation of the circumstances that led to the collision.

The Tennessee Highway Patrol is examining the crash and gathering evidence, while officials have emphasized the importance of establishing the facts before reaching conclusions.

The road involved has a posted speed limit of 50 mph. Investigators are expected to consider witness accounts and other evidence as they reconstruct the sequence of events.

Tennessee Highway Patrol Major Roy Brown acknowledged that the families and university community are looking for answers, but stressed that investigators need to complete their work before those answers can be provided.

The loss is particularly painful because Milligan's cyclists compete at a high level rather than simply riding recreationally. Earlier this year, the university's men's cycling team won the team time trial national championship at the USA Cycling Collegiate Road Nationals in Wisconsin.

That achievement now stands in stark contrast to the circumstances confronting the program.

Milligan President Stephen Waers has called on students and staff to support one another as the university deals with the deaths and the serious injuries. Counseling and pastoral support have also been made available.

The crash has inevitably renewed wider discussion about cyclist safety. Training rides require athletes to use public roads alongside motor vehicles, leaving even experienced groups vulnerable to collisions.

For Milligan, however, the immediate concern is much closer to home: two young students have lost their lives, several teammates remain hospitalized, and their friends, families and coaches are trying to comprehend what happened.

As the investigation continues, authorities have yet to establish publicly all of the factors behind the collision. What is already clear is that the Milligan cycling community has suffered an extraordinary loss, with the futures of two young athletes cut tragically short.

articles.title: Woman arrested for planning to attack the New York State Capitol: she pledged allegiance to the Islamic State
articles.standfirst: According to the FBI, she is accused of providing material support to the Islamic State
articles.summary: According to the FBI, she is accused of providing material support to the Islamic State
articles.body:
U.S. authorities have detained this Thursday a woman accused of planning a bomb attack against the Capitol of New York state, as reported by the network ‘Fox News’.

Jessica Bownie , 35, a resident of Albany, the state capital, is accused of attempting to provide material support to the Islamic State . According to the FBI, she confessed that her intention was to conceal a bomb in a DoorDash food delivery bag and carry out the attack while the senators were gathered.

Bownie conducted surveillance on at least five separate occasions over the course of a month around the Capitol, taking photographs and analyzing the security of the area, according to the FBI.

"The intention of the detainee was “to flee to Syria to join other territories controlled by ISIS,” as the FBI has confirmed on its social media.

Kash Patel, FBI chief: “The attack was already in an advanced stage”

By mid-July, the arrested woman contacted an FBI informant posing as an Islamic State facilitator to ask for help in making explosives and revealed her intentions to him.

Kash Patel , head of the FBI, said on his social media that “the attack was already in an advanced stage.” He therefore thanked the federal officers for having been able to prevent “another alleged terrorist attack.”

For her part, the state's governor, Kathy Hochul , thanked both the FBI and the local police who carried out Bownie's arrest and recalled that, given the increase in threats against public officials, security at the Capitol and throughout the state government had been strengthened.

Patel himself has also positively assessed the work of his colleagues for managing to prevent “more than 400 attacks of this kind so far in 2026”, although he clarified that this figure includes countries other than the United States.

articles.title: What is the Stop Social Security Garnishment Act and how can your benefits change if approved?
articles.standfirst: The legislation targets a growing concern over Social Security benefits and federal debt collection
articles.summary: The legislation targets a growing concern over Social Security benefits and federal debt collection
articles.body:
A growing number of older Americans carrying student loan debt could face a new financial challenge as federal collection efforts resume, but a proposed bill from Sen. Bernie Sanders could prevent Social Security benefits from being used to recover unpaid loans.

The Vermont senator is introducing the Stop Social Security Garnishment Act of 2026, legislation designed to block the Education Department from withholding Social Security retirement or disability payments from borrowers who have fallen behind on federal student loans.

The proposal would specifically prevent the government from reducing Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits to collect outstanding student debt, while allowing older Americans to keep access to money needed for everyday expenses.

Sanders said seniors should not have their benefits reduced because of student loans, particularly as many already face rising costs for healthcare, medication, food and housing.

“In the richest country in the history of the world, no senior should have their Social Security payments taken away from them to pay back student debt,” Sanders said.

“This is especially true when seniors throughout the country already cannot afford the skyrocketing price of healthcare, prescription drugs, groceries and housing. Congress must pass this legislation.”

The bill is expected to be introduced in the Senate when lawmakers return from recess on September 14. Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Ed Markey of Massachusetts are supporting the legislation as co-sponsors.

Why older borrowers are at center of debate

Student loan debt is no longer only an issue affecting younger Americans. A significant portion of borrowers are now approaching retirement age or already receiving Social Security benefits.

Around one in five student loan borrowers are at least 50 years old, according to data cited by Sanders ’ office and the Education Data Initiative. Borrowers between ages 50 and 61 have the highest average balance, with outstanding debt averaging approximately $48,875.

The senator’s office also noted that more than one-third of Social Security recipients with student loans rely on their monthly benefits to cover essential expenses.

Meanwhile, millions of Americans remain behind on federal student loan payments. Sanders ’ office estimates that more than nine million borrowers are currently in default, leaving many vulnerable to federal collection actions.

The proposed legislation would not cancel student loan debt or eliminate repayment obligations. Instead, it would remove Social Security garnishment as a collection method for borrowers who depend on those payments.

What happens if Stop Social Security Garnishment Act isn't passed?

The Education Department previously delayed involuntary collections on federal student loans while new repayment options were being implemented.

The changes followed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act , signed into law in July 2025, which reduced the number of repayment plans available to borrowers and introduced new repayment structures.

The department said the pause would give borrowers time to review their options and begin the rehabilitation process if they were in default. However, Sanders warned that restarting collections could put additional pressure on seniors already dealing with higher living costs.

The Stop Social Security Garnishment Act now faces the challenge of moving through Congress before any protections become law. Until then, older borrowers with student debt remain closely watching how lawmakers address the issue.

articles.title: Student Loans Forgiveness 2026: How can you get your debt erased or make a better repayment plan
articles.standfirst: New repayment rules could change how Americans lower payments or qualify for debt relief
articles.summary: New repayment rules could change how Americans lower payments or qualify for debt relief
articles.body:
The student loan landscape has entered another major transition in 2026, leaving millions of borrowers searching for answers about forgiveness, repayment options and how to avoid costly mistakes.

More than 40 million Americans are carrying federal student loan debt , and recent changes have made it increasingly important for borrowers to understand exactly where they stand.

New repayment plans, updated forgiveness rules and possible tax consequences mean the strategy that worked previously may no longer be the best route forward.

While student loan forgiveness remains available through several federal programs, qualifying is not automatic. Borrowers must understand their loan type, repayment plan and eligibility requirements before making major decisions.

The first step is reviewing your federal student aid account to confirm your outstanding balance, loan history and current repayment plan. Changes introduced in 2026 mean factors such as when loans were issued can determine which repayment options are available.

How borrowers can qualify for student loan forgiveness

There is no universal program that wipes away all federal student loan debt . Instead, borrowers must apply through individual forgiveness programs based on their circumstances.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness remains one of the most significant options for eligible borrowers.

The program allows qualifying employees who work full-time for government agencies or nonprofit organizations to have their remaining Direct Loan balance forgiven after completing 120 qualifying monthly payments.

Other programs, including Teacher Loan Forgiveness and certain discharge options, can provide relief for borrowers who meet specific requirements.

However, choosing the correct repayment plan is now a crucial part of the process. The introduction of the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) and Tiered Standard Plan has changed how some borrowers approach their monthly payments.

Borrowers should also continue tracking their progress carefully by keeping copies of payment records, employment certifications and forgiveness applications.

Many forgiveness programs take years to complete, and mistakes along the way can delay approval.

Repayment choices and tax rules could affect debt relief

Finding a lower monthly payment does not always mean finding the best long-term solution. Some borrowers may need to consider the impact repayment choices have on taxes, deductions and future forgiveness eligibility.

The Repayment Assistance Plan calculates payments using income and family details, meaning factors such as marital status can affect what a borrower owes.

Some married borrowers may consider filing taxes separately because it could reduce how much spouse income is included in repayment calculations.

However, that decision can come with trade-offs, including a potentially higher tax bill and losing access to certain benefits such as the student loan interest deduction.

Borrowers should also pay attention to the tax implications of forgiven debt. The temporary federal tax protection that excluded many forgiven student loans from taxable income expired after 2025.

As a result, some borrowers receiving forgiveness in 2026 could face tax obligations unless they qualify for an exception.

Certain programs, including Public Service Loan Forgiveness and Teacher Loan Forgiveness , may continue to receive favorable tax treatment under federal rules.

Beyond forgiveness, borrowers should look for other ways to reduce the financial pressure of student debt.

Eligible borrowers may qualify for the student loan interest deduction, while some employers offer education assistance programs that can include student loan repayment benefits.

Refinancing may also appear appealing, but borrowers with federal loans should carefully consider the consequences.

Moving federal loans into private refinancing can mean losing access to forgiveness programs, income-based repayment options and other federal protections.

With student loan rules continuing to evolve, the best approach in 2026 is not making quick changes without understanding the long-term impact. Borrowers who review their options carefully may find a path toward lower payments, debt relief or a more manageable repayment plan.

articles.title: What are the hidden benefits of 100% VA disability? Everything you can get besides the monthly payment
articles.standfirst: Many veterans miss out on available education, healthcare and money-saving programs
articles.summary: Many veterans miss out on available education, healthcare and money-saving programs
articles.body:
A 100 percent VA disability rating is often associated with one key benefit which is a higher monthly tax-free payment. However, the designation can also unlock a wide range of additional programs that may significantly impact a veteran’s healthcare, finances and family support.

Many veterans are unaware that a total disability rating can provide access to benefits that go well beyond compensation.

Some are available directly through the Department of Veterans Affairs , while others depend on whether the veteran has a permanent and total (P&T) designation, eligible dependents or lives in a state that offers additional veteran assistance.

Understanding these benefits can help veterans make sure they are receiving the full support available after years of service.

Healthcare, housing and employment benefits tied to 100 percent rating

One of the most valuable benefits connected to a 100 percent VA disability rating is expanded healthcare coverage.

Veterans with a total service-connected disability rating may qualify for no-cost VA healthcare and prescription medications. They may also be eligible for travel reimbursement when attending approved appointments at VA medical facilities or authorized healthcare locations.

Dental care is another benefit that stands out. Unlike many lower-rated veterans who have limited dental eligibility, veterans with a 100 percent service-connected disability rating generally qualify for comprehensive VA dental care .

The rating can also provide financial advantages when purchasing a home. Eligible veterans may receive a waiver of the VA home loan funding fee , which can save thousands of dollars during a home purchase or refinance.

Additional opportunities include a 10-point preference when applying for federal employment and access to Veteran Readiness and Employment services , which can help veterans pursue career training, education and employment support.

Veterans with eligible dependents may also qualify for additional monthly compensation. These benefits can increase based on qualifying spouses, children or other dependent circumstances.

Overlooked programs available to veterans

A 100 percent permanent and total disability rating can create important opportunities for a veteran’s family.

One of the most significant programs is Dependents’ Educational Assistance (DEA), which can provide monthly education benefits to eligible spouses and children of veterans who are permanently and totally disabled.

Families may also qualify for CHAMPVA, a healthcare program that helps cover medical costs for eligible spouses and children who are not covered by TRICARE.

Another frequently overlooked benefit involves student loans. Veterans who meet Department of Education requirements for Total and Permanent Disability discharge may be eligible to have qualifying federal student loans forgiven.

Beyond federal programs, many states provide additional benefits for veterans rated 100 percent disabled. These can include property tax exemptions, reduced vehicle fees, education assistance for dependents, recreational benefits and discounts on hunting or fishing licenses.

Some veterans may also gain access to military-related resources, including commissaries, exchanges, recreational facilities and other programs depending on their eligibility status.

A 100 percent VA disability rating represents more than a monthly payment. It can provide a network of healthcare protections, financial assistance and family benefits designed to support veterans after their service.

Because eligibility rules vary depending on disability status, dependents, state laws and whether a veteran is considered permanent and total, veterans should review their individual benefits with the VA and local veterans assistance offices.

articles.title: SNAP E&T Program: What is it, how much in benefits you'll get and how to apply?
articles.standfirst: Eligible participants could receive education support, supplies and help finding work
articles.summary: Eligible participants could receive education support, supplies and help finding work
articles.body:
Receiving SNAP benefits can help millions of Americans manage their grocery costs, but many participants may not realize the program also connects them with employment resources designed to create long-term opportunities.

The SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) program is designed to help eligible recipients develop job skills, gain work experience and overcome barriers that may prevent them from finding stable employment.

Instead of providing additional food assistance, SNAP E&T focuses on education, career preparation and practical support that can help participants move toward financial independence.

Every state operates a SNAP E&T program using federal funding, but the services available can differ depending on location and local workforce needs.

What does SNAP E&T provide and how much money can participants receive?

SNAP E&T doesn't work like traditional SNAP benefits , meaning there is no set monthly payment amount that every participant receives.

Instead, the program provides services and reimbursements for costs connected to participation. Eligible participants may receive assistance with expenses that are reasonable, necessary and directly related to completing their training or employment plan. Support available through SNAP E&T may include:

Help searching for and securing employment

Transportation assistance, such as bus passes or gas cards

Career planning and job counseling

Books, training materials and educational supplies

Work uniforms, tools and other employment-related equipment

Childcare assistance in some states

The program can also provide case management, helping participants identify career goals and choose training opportunities that match their interests and local job market needs.

Someone using SNAP E&T may decide to return to school, gain certification for a new career or develop skills needed to advance in their current field.

Who qualifies for SNAP Employment and Training?

Eligibility requirements vary by state, but participants generally need to meet a few basic conditions. Most applicants must:

Not receive TANF cash assistance

Be able to work after completing the program

Some states also require certain SNAP recipients to participate in employment and training activities as a condition of keeping their benefits.

If participation is mandatory, the SNAP recipient will receive information from their eligibility worker explaining the rules they must follow. The notice will also explain whether there are valid reasons someone may be excused from participation.

Reasons for exemption may include situations such as illness, a household emergency, caring for an ill family member or transportation problems that make participation difficult.

How do you apply for SNAP E&T?

Anyone interested in SNAP Employment and Training should begin by contacting their SNAP caseworker or local SNAP office.

Because every state manages its own program differently, applicants will need to check their state’s SNAP E&T resources to find available providers, training options and specific eligibility requirements.

SNAP E&T can be an important pathway for people who want to improve their employment prospects while receiving assistance.

By offering training, career guidance and help with everyday barriers, the program aims to give participants the tools needed to find work and build greater financial stability.

articles.title: Pa. college soccer player fatally stabbed by boyfriend who enlisted mom to help hide body
articles.standfirst: The incoming PennWest soccer player was found dead in the back of her Jeep after her family requested a welfare check
articles.summary: The incoming PennWest soccer player was found dead in the back of her Jeep after her family requested a welfare check
articles.body:
Karoline Heintz, an 18-year-old Pennsylvania soccer player preparing to begin college, was fatally stabbed by her boyfriend, who investigators say later enlisted his mother to help conceal the killing.

Heintz was found inside the rear hatch of her Jeep Cherokee shortly after midnight Thursday near the California Public Library in California, Pennsylvania . Police launched a welfare check after her family became concerned when she failed to return as expected.

Heintz had recently graduated from Peters Township High School and was preparing to begin her freshman year at PennWest California. She was listed as a defender on the university’s women’s soccer roster, with the team scheduled to open its 2026 season on Aug. 29.

According to investigators, Heintz left her home at about 9:30 p.m. Wednesday and met her boyfriend, 18-year-old Royce Moser , outside his father’s residence in North Strabane Township. The pair reportedly began discussing their relationship and how they would handle it as Heintz started college.

Police allege the conversation became heated. Moser then went inside the home and retrieved a large kitchen knife before returning to Heintz’s vehicle.

Investigators say he told her he had something for her before allegedly stabbing her in the chest. He then allegedly placed her body in the Jeep’s rear hatch and drove to his mother’s residence in Beallsville.

Police say mother helped conceal the killing

Investigators allege Rachel Moser helped her son clean the Jeep and remove potential evidence. Police say she supplied latex gloves and followed Royce as he drove Heintz’s vehicle toward California Borough. The Jeep was eventually abandoned near the library, with Heintz still inside.

Authorities say Royce later told his mother that he believed a “demon” had taken over and instructed him to hurt Heintz. Police haven't said whether he has a documented mental health history or whether such an issue played any role in the alleged attack.

The investigation moved quickly after Heintz’s family reported concerns about her whereabouts. Her father reportedly tracked her location and noticed that she had stopped at Moser’s residence. Surveillance footage also allegedly captured the Jeep traveling toward the library while another vehicle followed behind.

Officers subsequently discovered Heintz’s body inside the blood-stained vehicle. Pennsylvania State Police Trooper Rocco Gagliardi said investigators were able to make significant progress within hours of the discovery.

Moser faces homicide, evidence-tampering, abuse-of-a-corpse, conspiracy and obstruction charges. His mother faces charges including hindering the apprehension of a fugitive, tampering with evidence, abuse of a corpse, conspiracy and obstruction.

The allegations haven't been proven in court.

PennWest expressed heartbreak over Heintz’s death, extending condolences to her family, friends and teammates.

articles.title: Reports claim Bill Clinton is reviewing end-of-life plans as he turns 80, but questions remain
articles.standfirst: The reported plans include a traditional funeral service befitting a former commander-in-chief
articles.summary: The reported plans include a traditional funeral service befitting a former commander-in-chief
articles.body:
F ormer President Bill Clinton celebrated his 80th birthday on August 19, but a recent report has sparked widespread discussion about his health and future planning. According to RadarOnline, Clinton and former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton have reportedly begun reviewing and organizing future end-of-life arrangements, including potential updates to the former president’s estate plans. The report, which relies on unnamed sources, has not been independently confirmed by the Clinton family.

The claims have nevertheless generated significant attention online, particularly given Clinton’s age and well-documented medical history. According to the report, Hillary Clinton , 78, has allegedly started organizing plans for a future memorial service that could take place at Washington National Cathedral in Washington, D.C. The reported plans include a traditional funeral service befitting a former commander-in-chief.

While the details remain speculative, the discussion has highlighted an often-overlooked reality: state funeral preparations are routinely maintained for living former presidents. In the past, spokesperson Elizabeth Hargrove confirmed that such plans exist for all surviving former U.S. presidents.

Clinton has a long history of heart-related health issues

The report also suggested that Clinton could ultimately be laid to rest in Little Rock, Arkansas, at the presidential library that bears his name. Presidential historian Leon Wagener has previously suggested that Clinton might prefer the library’s rooftop garden as a burial site, though no official decision has ever been publicly announced.

The renewed attention comes against the backdrop of Clinton’s long history of heart-related health issues. In 2004, he underwent quadruple bypass surgery after doctors discovered significant heart disease. Six years later, he returned to the hospital for a procedure to insert stents and open a blocked coronary artery.

More recently, Clinton spent nearly a week hospitalized in 2021 while being treated for a urinary tract infection that had spread to his bloodstream. Public concern resurfaced last year after photographs appeared to show Clinton carrying what some observers believed was a portable medical device. However, no official statement indicated that he was facing a new health crisis at the time.

Scrutiny and public pressure

Despite those past medical challenges, Clinton has continued to make public appearances and has remained active in political and charitable events. The RadarOnline report also claimed that ongoing public scrutiny has contributed to concerns about Clinton’s health.

In recent years, Clinton’s past association with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein has continued to attract media attention following the release of court documents and renewed public interest in the case. Clinton has repeatedly stated that he was unaware of Epstein’s criminal activities and has denied any wrongdoing.

Medical experts frequently note that prolonged stress can have an impact on cardiovascular health. Dr. Stuart Fischer, who has not treated Clinton , has previously explained that severe psychological stress can place additional strain on the heart and circulatory system. However, there is no public evidence indicating that Clinton is currently experiencing a medical emergency or that any specific stress-related condition has been diagnosed.

As reports about the alleged funeral planning circulated around Clinton’s 80th birthday , reactions on social media were mixed. Many users focused on celebrating the milestone, with one supporter writing, “Happy birthday, Frmr Prez Clinton! We had the best economy & no deficit during your administration.”

articles.title: Max Social Security Benefit 2027: How much will you receive with the latest COLA projection for next year?
articles.standfirst: A projected 3.6% increase could lift Social Security payments in 2027, but the biggest possible check depends on more than the annual COLA
articles.summary: A projected 3.6% increase could lift Social Security payments in 2027, but the biggest possible check depends on more than the annual COLA
articles.body:
S ocial Security recipients are beginning to look ahead to 2027 as new inflation data provides a clearer picture of how much benefits could rise next year.

The latest projection from the Senior Citizens League puts the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) at 3.6%. That estimate is slightly above the 3.5% projection published by AARP using earlier inflation data, but neither figure is official yet.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) will calculate the final COLA using Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) data from July, August and September.

The agency is expected to announce the official adjustment in October, with the increase applying to benefits paid in January 2027.

That means retirees should treat the current projections as estimates rather than guaranteed increases.

For someone receiving the maximum 2026 retirement benefit of $5,181 per month at age 70, a 3.6% increase would produce an illustrative payment of about $5,368 per month in 2027. That's an increase of roughly $187 per month, or about $2,244 over a full year.

However, that calculation should not be interpreted as the final 2027 maximum benefit. The actual maximum payment for people newly claiming benefits can change based on the Social Security benefit formula and other annual adjustments.

Who can actually receive the maximum Social Security benefit?

The maximum Social Security check is reserved for a relatively small group of workers. Simply having a high salary shortly before retirement isn't enough.

To qualify for the maximum retirement benefit, a worker generally needs to have earned at or above Social Security 's maximum taxable earnings level for many years and claim benefits at an age that produces the largest possible payment.

The SSA's own examples show how strongly claiming age affects the benefit. A worker with maximum taxable earnings throughout their career can receive substantially more by waiting until age 70 rather than claiming at 62.

The distinction is important because the COLA applies to existing benefit amounts. It does not suddenly give every recipient the maximum payment.

For example, a retiree receiving $2,000 per month who receives a 3.6% COLA would see an increase of approximately $72, bringing the payment to about $2,072. Someone receiving $3,000 would gain approximately $108 and move to roughly $3,108.

The latest estimates therefore matter more as a percentage than as a single universal dollar amount.

Recent data also shows why projections have been changing. The 2026 COLA was 2.8%, while the latest 3.6% estimate would represent the largest increase since the 8.7% adjustment associated with 2023 benefits. It would still be nowhere near the record 14.3% COLA in 1981, when inflation was dramatically higher.

Another important consideration is Medicare . For many beneficiaries, Medicare premiums are deducted directly from Social Security payments, meaning the amount that ultimately reaches a bank account can differ from the gross benefit increase.

The SSA says the official 2027 COLA will not be known until the October announcement.

For now, 3.6% is a useful working estimate, while AARP's 3.5% projection demonstrates how quickly forecasts can move as new inflation figures arrive.

If the 3.6% projection holds, a person already receiving $5,181 a month could see a payment of approximately $5,368, but only people who already qualify for the maximum benefit will be in that position. For most retirees, the actual increase will depend on their individual Social Security benefit.

The final number will come after September's inflation data is available and the SSA completes its calculation in October.

articles.standfirst: Costco is entering the Medicare market, but the price and launch date of its new plans have not yet been revealed
articles.summary: Costco is entering the Medicare market, but the price and launch date of its new plans have not yet been revealed
articles.body:
C ostco is preparing to make a major move into the healthcare insurance market, with the retailer set to offer its own co-branded Medicare products through a partnership with nonprofit insurer SCAN Group.

The announcement has generated considerable interest among older Americans, particularly Costco members who may be wondering how much the plans will cost and when they can actually sign up.

The short answer is that Costco has not yet announced specific premiums, deductibles or other out-of-pocket costs for the new plans.

The company and SCAN also have not publicly identified the exact states where the initial products will be offered or provided a firm enrollment date. The launch remains subject to regulatory approval.

The partnership, announced August 18, 2026, will initially involve Medicare Advantage plans in two states and a Medicare Supplement , or Medigap, product in a third.

The companies are targeting a potential market of roughly five million Medicare beneficiaries during the initial rollout.

That means consumers should be careful about headlines suggesting that a particular Costco Medicare plan already has a confirmed price. Those details have not been finalized publicly.

What could Costco's Medicare plans include?

The proposed offering is designed to combine SCAN's experience in Medicare insurance with Costco's existing healthcare infrastructure.

Potential benefits could include access to pharmacy services, over-the-counter products, vision care and hearing-related benefits, although the precise benefits will depend on the individual plans ultimately approved by federal regulators.

Costco already has an established relationship with Medicare Advantage beneficiaries through its retail operations.

The retailer says it accepts Medicare Advantage prepaid benefits cards at its registers, with eligible cards potentially covering items such as over-the-counter products, vitamins, hearing and optical products and certain food purchases, depending on the individual's insurance plan.

The new insurance products would be different from simply using an existing Medicare Advantage card at Costco, however.

They would be insurance plans offered in partnership with SCAN, rather than a new Medicare benefit automatically available to every Costco member.

Another important point is that a Costco membership will not simply be bundled into the Medicare insurance plan.

Federal rules restrict Medicare Advantage insurers from offering certain non-health-related incentives as part of a plan, and reports indicate that the new coverage will not include a Costco membership.

When will Costco Medicare plans be available?

The exact launch date remains unknown. Costco and SCAN must receive the necessary regulatory approval before the products can be sold, meaning prospective customers will need to wait for further details.

The timing is particularly significant because Medicare Advantage plans operate on an annual cycle. CMS has already finalized its payment policies for 2027, with the agency projecting a 2.48% average increase in payments to Medicare Advantage plans compared with 2026.

Once Costco and SCAN disclose their approved plans, consumers will need to compare them against other Medicare Advantage and Medigap options available in their area.

Premiums are only one part of that calculation: provider networks, prescription coverage, deductibles, copayments, annual out-of-pocket limits and additional benefits can all substantially affect the overall value of a plan.

For now, therefore, there is no confirmed Costco Medicare premium to quote and no definitive nationwide launch date. The initial rollout is expected to be limited, with expansion potentially following if the pilot proves successful.

Prospective customers can monitor Costco's healthcare partnerships and Medicare information from CMS for official updates as the plans move through the approval process.

articles.title: Charter plane crashes near remote Alaska military site, killing all 8 on board
articles.standfirst: The civilian-contracted aircraft crashed near its destination
articles.summary: The civilian-contracted aircraft crashed near its destination
articles.body:
A charter aircraft carrying eight people crashed near a remote military installation in western Alaska, killing everyone on board, according to military officials and search-and-rescue teams.

The flight departed Anchorage and was headed to Cape Newenham, a U.S. Air Force radar site located roughly 450 miles southwest of the state's largest city. Officials said the civilian-contracted aircraft crashed near its destination, prompting an immediate search-and-recovery operation.

The Alaska Command confirmed that the aircraft was carrying two pilots and six passengers. Rescuers later reached the crash site and determined there were no survivors. “This is a devastating loss for our military family and the communities we serve,” U.S. Air Force Lieutenant General Robert Davis said in a statement. “These individuals were dedicated professionals carrying out a vital mission in a demanding environment.”

Challenging conditions surrounding Cape Newenham Airport

Authorities have not yet released the identities of the victims. Military officials said the names of the passengers and crew will be made public only after family members have been notified. The tragedy has drawn attention to the challenging conditions surrounding Cape Newenham Airport, one of Alaska's most remote airfields.

The airport serves a radar installation that is part of the region's air defense network and is restricted to military and approved charter flights. The airstrip features a gravel runway measuring nearly 4,000 feet in length and sits on the slope of a mountain rising more than 2,300 feet above sea level.

Aviation experts have long noted the unique challenges posed by the location, where high terrain flanks both sides of the runway. Pilots operating in the area must navigate difficult approaches, and aviation guides have described landing options as extremely limited once an aircraft passes certain approach points.

Supporting the victims' families, the priority

While investigators have not suggested that terrain or weather played a role in the crash, the conditions highlight the demanding environment faced by crews operating in remote regions of Alaska. Davis emphasized that supporting the victims' families remains the military's primary focus in the aftermath of the disaster.

“Our absolute priority right now is providing unwavering support to their families, friends, and teammates during this devastating time,” he said.

“We are profoundly grateful for the swift and tireless response of our search and recovery professionals.” The crash also prompted an outpouring of condolences from elected officials across the state.

Alaska Senator Lisa Murkowski expressed her sympathies in a post on X, noting her familiarity with aviation operations throughout the state.

“I’ve traveled extensively with Security Aviation throughout Alaska, and have met many of their experienced pilots,” Murkowski wrote.

Alaska's vast geography and sparse transportation infrastructure make air travel essential for many communities, government agencies, and military operations. Charter flights routinely connect remote locations that are inaccessible by road, often requiring crews to operate in some of the most challenging flying conditions in North America.

articles.standfirst: Saturday night's Powerball draw carries an estimated $68 million top prize, with the winning numbers still pending
articles.summary: Saturday night's Powerball draw carries an estimated $68 million top prize, with the winning numbers still pending
articles.body:
P owerball players across the United States are waiting for the winning numbers from the Saturday, August 22, 2026 drawing, with an estimated $68 million jackpot up for grabs.

At the time of writing, the official Powerball website lists the August 22 drawing as “Results Pending,” meaning the winning combination has not yet been officially posted. The estimated cash value of the jackpot is approximately $29.2 million.

That means players should be cautious about social media posts or unofficial websites claiming to have the final numbers before the official result is published. Powerball's own draw-results page remains the authoritative source for the winning combination.

The jackpot has reached $68 million after there was no jackpot winner in the previous drawing on Wednesday, August 19. That draw produced the numbers 10, 21, 58, 61, 64 and Powerball 17, with a 2X Power Play. No ticket matched all six numbers required to claim the jackpot.

What are the Powerball numbers for August 22?

The winning numbers for Saturday, August 22, 2026 have not yet been officially released.

The official Powerball website currently shows:

- White balls: Results pending

- Powerball: Results pending

- Power Play: Results pending

- Estimated jackpot: $68 million

- Estimated cash value: $29.2 million

The Powerball drawing is held three times a week, on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, giving players several opportunities to compete for the growing jackpot. A standard play costs $2, while the Power Play option costs an additional $1 and can multiply eligible non-jackpot prizes.

Players need to match all five white numbers and the red Powerball to win the jackpot. There are also eight other prize tiers, meaning a ticket does not necessarily have to match all six numbers to win money.

The odds of winning the Powerball jackpot are extraordinarily low at approximately 1 in 292.2 million. However, the game offers smaller prizes for different combinations, with prizes starting at $4.

Previous Powerball results

The most recent drawing before Saturday's event took place on Wednesday, August 19.

There was no jackpot winner, helping push the estimated prize to $68 million for Saturday.

The cash option attached to a jackpot can be considerably smaller than the advertised annuity value. For Saturday's drawing, official Powerball information puts the estimated cash value at about $29.2 million.

A jackpot winner can generally choose between receiving the advertised annuity through a series of payments or taking the cash option, with taxes applying to lottery winnings.

For anyone holding a ticket for Saturday night's draw, checking the numbers against the official Powerball results is particularly important. Winning tickets must be validated and claimed according to the rules of the jurisdiction where they were purchased.

The key point for now is that there is no confirmed winning combination for August 22 available yet.

Once the drawing takes place and the numbers are verified, the official Powerball results page will provide the definitive numbers and information on whether the $68 million jackpot was won or rolls over to the next drawing.

articles.title: Department of Education Student Loan Forgiveness Reversal: what is the new requirement to get your student debt erased?
articles.standfirst: Teachers, nurses and other public workers could face months or years of additional repayment before forgiveness
articles.summary: Teachers, nurses and other public workers could face months or years of additional repayment before forgiveness
articles.body:
A borrower can spend a decade planning around Public Service Loan Forgiveness , only to discover that the finish line has suddenly moved.

That is the concern now facing some teachers, nurses, government employees and nonprofit workers after the Department of Education began reversing qualifying PSLF payments that had previously appeared on their accounts.

The department says the changes are not a new restriction on forgiveness. Instead, Federal Student Aid identified what it describes as coding and payment-count errors tied to changes made in May 2024, and it is now correcting those records.

That distinction matters. PSLF still requires 120 qualifying monthly payments while a borrower works full-time for an eligible public service employer. But if previously credited months are removed, affected borrowers may have to keep paying until their corrected total reaches 120.

“The Department remains committed to ensuring that every qualifying payment is properly credited to a borrower’s account,” an Education Department spokesperson said.

What borrowers now need to do for PSLF forgiveness

There's no new application threshold or extra payment beyond the existing 120-payment requirement.

The practical change is that some borrowers may no longer be as close to forgiveness as they believed. If qualifying credits disappear from a StudentAid.gov account, the borrower may need to make additional eligible payments before the remaining balance can be erased.

Financial literacy instructor Alex Beene told Newsweek the situation is best understood as a recalculation rather than a replacement of PSLF.

“For public-service borrowers, this is not a new restriction on PSLF itself, but a correction of payment-counting errors dating to changes Federal Student Aid made in 2024,” Beene said.

Borrower advocates, however, argue that the consequences are more serious than a routine technical adjustment.

“This unprecedented reversal may require teachers, nurses, service members, and other public service workers to make years of additional student loan payments before obtaining the debt relief guaranteed under PSLF; it might even result in reinstated loans,” Protect Borrowers said in a statement.

American Federation of Teachers president Randi Weingarten added: “The Department of Education needs to ensure no public service worker pays the price for someone else’s mistake.”

Could already forgiven loans be reinstated?

That remains one of the biggest unanswered questions. Advocacy groups have warned that reversing PSLF credit could eventually threaten loans that have already been forgiven.

The Education Department, however, hasn't publicly said that it intends to reinstate discharged balances, and such a broad move would be highly unusual.

Borrowers still working toward PSLF have a more immediate task: check their qualifying payment count on StudentAid.gov and compare it with previous records.

Anyone who sees months disappear should keep copies of employment certifications, prior payment histories and earlier PSLF counts in case they need to dispute the change.

The underlying PSLF rules remain the same, but the new reality is more unsettling. Borrowers who thought they were months away from debt relief may now find themselves with a much longer repayment timeline.

articles.title: Seattle radio station Kiro News claims the powerful and wealthy are protecting Bill Gates' daughter
articles.standfirst: The Phia co-founder is under scrutiny over affiliate practices
articles.summary: The Phia co-founder is under scrutiny over affiliate practices
articles.body:
The most striking part of the controversy surrounding Phoebe Gates may not be what her startup is accused of doing, but how little attention the story has attracted outside business and technology circles.

That was the argument made by KIRO fill-in hosts Angela Poe Russell and Jim Dever , who questioned whether Gates ’ family name has softened the scrutiny surrounding Phia , the AI shopping company she co-founded with Sophia Kianni .

Bloomberg has reported that Phia used a practice known as cookie stuffing, which can allow a company to claim affiliate commissions for purchases it didn't actually generate.

Internal Slack messages cited in the reporting indicated that the founders were aware of concerns surrounding the practice months before Phia publicly described the issue as a recently discovered bug.

“Bias is not just how you cover a story and how you report it — it’s who you choose to pay attention to and who you ignore,” Russell said on The John Curley Show.

Phia has denied intentionally committing fraud and said features that caused misattributions were removed. The company has also said it is reviewing transactions and issuing reversals to affected brand partners.

Is Gates getting special treatment?

The discussion quickly turned from Phia ’s business practices to the influence that can come with being the daughter of Bill and Melinda Gates .

KIRO producer Joe Wallace said he would be surprised if Phoebe Gates faced severe consequences even if wrongdoing were eventually established.

“I would be surprised if she faces anything beyond a financial penalty, and probably not even a big one,” Wallace said.

Asked why, he responded: “Because she’s the daughter of Bill Gates, and they have an ungodly amount of wealth at their disposal.”

“And power,” Dever added.

Those comments are opinion, not evidence that Gates ’ family wealth has influenced any regulator, investigation or media organization. Neither Gates nor Kianni has been criminally charged over the reported affiliate practices.

Still, the financial consequences for Phia have already been significant. Bloomberg reported that average daily revenue fell sharply after the disputed tracking features were disabled, while affiliate platform Impact.com suspended the company from its marketplace.

Secretive Stanford course draws fresh attention

The KIRO hosts also pointed to Gates ’ time at Stanford, where she participated in an unofficial, invitation-only program called “So You Think You Can Rule the World?”

The course reportedly accepted just 12 students and focused on power structures, networking and navigating complex systems. Former participants have described it as highly selective and secretive.

“It was a handpicked group of 12 students,” Dever said. “They weren’t allowed to talk about it.”

The class has gained renewed attention because Gates later used relationships built at Stanford while developing Phia . The startup launched in 2025 and went on to raise tens of millions of dollars from prominent investors.

None of that proves improper influence. But for Russell , the wider question remains whether a less connected founder facing the same allegations would have escaped such an intense national spotlight.

“This is the daughter of one of the wealthiest people in the world,” she said.
