articles.title: When can you start collecting Social Security and what is the biggest payment you can get?
articles.standfirst: Claiming Social Security at 62 can provide income sooner, but waiting until 70 can substantially increase your monthly benefit
articles.summary: Claiming Social Security at 62 can provide income sooner, but waiting until 70 can substantially increase your monthly benefit
articles.body:
S ocial Security retirement benefits can become an important source of income in retirement, but deciding when to claim them is one of the biggest financial choices many Americans face.

The earliest age at which most people can begin collecting their own retirement benefit is 62, provided they have accumulated enough Social Security -covered work history. The Social Security Administration generally requires 40 credits, which is equivalent to about 10 years of work.

However, claiming at 62 does not mean receiving the full amount a worker has earned through their career. Starting benefits before full retirement age results in a permanent reduction in the monthly payment.

For people whose full retirement age is 67, claiming at 62 can mean receiving only about 70% of the benefit they would have received at full retirement age. Fidelity notes that claiming at 62 can result in a reduction of as much as 30%, depending on the worker's circumstances.

That creates a significant trade-off: taking Social Security earlier means collecting payments for more years, while waiting produces larger monthly checks later.

Waiting until 70 can deliver the biggest monthly benefit

Full retirement age depends on the year you were born. For people born in 1960 or later, it is 67. Workers can claim before reaching that age, but their benefit is reduced. Conversely, someone who waits beyond full retirement age can earn delayed retirement credits.

The increase continues until age 70. There is no additional retirement benefit increase for waiting beyond 70.

Fidelity estimates that delaying Social Security beyond full retirement age can increase the benefit by roughly 8% for each year of additional waiting, making age 70 the point at which a worker can generally receive the largest monthly retirement payment based on their own record.

The actual maximum, however, is not a single figure that applies to everyone. It depends heavily on a worker's earnings history and the year in which they claim.

For 2026, the SSA says a worker who earned the maximum taxable amount in every year beginning at age 22 could receive:

- $2,969 per month if claiming at age 62.

- $4,152 per month if claiming at full retirement age.

- $5,181 per month if claiming at age 70.

That top figure works out to more than $62,000 a year before taxes if received for 12 months.

But very few workers qualify for the maximum. Social Security calculates retirement benefits largely from a worker's earnings record, and only earnings up to the annual taxable maximum count toward the calculation. In 2026, that taxable maximum is $184,500.

Why claiming at 62 isn't automatically the wrong choice

Although waiting can produce a much larger monthly payment, there is no universally correct claiming age.

Someone who needs the income immediately, has limited retirement savings or has health concerns may decide that collecting at 62 makes sense. On the other hand, someone with sufficient savings who expects to live well into their 80s or beyond may place greater value on maximizing their guaranteed monthly income.

Other considerations can include employment income, taxes, a spouse's benefits and survivor protection.

People who continue working while receiving Social Security before full retirement age can also face the earnings test. In 2026, the SSA says $1 in benefits can be withheld for every $2 earned above $24,480 for someone below full retirement age for the entire year. Different rules apply during the year a person reaches full retirement age.

It is also important not to confuse Social Security claiming age with Medicare enrollment. Someone who delays Social Security beyond 65 may still need to take action regarding Medicare to avoid potential penalties or gaps in coverage. The SSA specifically warns people delaying retirement benefits not to overlook Medicare enrollment.

articles.title: ‘You’re All That Matters’: Leaked letters between Trump and his aide Natalie Harp send shockwaves through Washington
articles.standfirst: Natalie Harp accompanies the U.S. president wherever he goes
articles.summary: Natalie Harp accompanies the U.S. president wherever he goes
articles.body:
The name of Natalie Harp has begun to be heard loudly in recent times. The secretary to the President Donald Trump is becoming increasingly important, and not because of the fact that she accompanies him wherever he goes with a portable printer to print the magnate's speeches on paper.

Now, it is known that the closeness between the two could not be greater , since she accompanies him everywhere, including among the small group of people who accompanied Trump on his secret escape from Air Force One , the presidential plane, when leaving Turkey after a NATO summit.

According to sources, an alleged romance between President Donald Trump and his secretary, Natalie Harp, is becoming increasingly likely. Not only does she appear to be his assistant, but some letters sent by Harp to Donald Trump in 2023 could point to a possible affair between them.

Natalie Harp, to Donald Trump: “I want things to always be good between us”

“ You are everything that matters to me,” Natalie wrote to him in a letter while Trump was trying to return to the Capitol for his second term.

“ I want things to always be good between us, (...) I know I’ve been distracted all week” , can be read in some excerpts from the letters. In addition, she shares confidences of a personal nature, such as expressing the way public opinion was affecting her: “Not because I care what others think, but because I see myself falling in your esteem and good opinion . You know, that is the fear I have, because I never want to bring you anything but joy”.

“If there is anything else I may have done to cause you discomfort, please forgive me. I know some people have said that I haven’t replied to their messages, and there have been some issues with the mobile phone at the international level,” could be read in one of the shared letters. This rapprochement between the two has not gone down very well at the White House since, according to sources in the North American country, “she is not liked by many.”

articles.title: VA Dental Benefits: What veterans are eligible for free dental care?
articles.standfirst: VA dental coverage is not automatic for every veteran, here are the eligibility classes that can unlock free treatment
articles.summary: VA dental coverage is not automatic for every veteran, here are the eligibility classes that can unlock free treatment
articles.body:
Serving in the U.S. military can provide access to a wide range of healthcare benefits, but veterans should not assume that enrollment in VA healthcare automatically means all dental treatment will be free.

The Department of Veterans Affairs uses a separate eligibility system for dental services. Veterans are placed into different dental benefit classes depending on factors including their service history, disability status, medical circumstances and living situation.

Some classes can qualify a veteran for comprehensive dental treatment, while others provide care only for a specific condition or purpose.

The VA's current guidance makes clear that qualifying veterans may receive some or all of their dental care through the department. However, the eligibility requirements for dental care are different from those for general VA medical benefits .

Which veterans can receive free VA dental care?

One of the broadest categories is Class I. Veterans who have a service-connected dental disability or condition for which they receive monthly compensation may qualify for any dental care they need.

Former prisoners of war can also qualify for comprehensive dental treatment under Class IIC. Meanwhile, veterans with one or more service-connected disabilities rated at 100% disabling may qualify under Class IV.

Veterans who receive disability compensation at the 100% rate because they are unemployable can also fall into this category, although the VA notes that a temporary 100% rating does not qualify for this particular dental benefit.

There are several other pathways to dental care.

Veterans with a service-connected but non-compensable dental condition, or a dental disability resulting from combat wounds or service trauma, may qualify under Class IIA.

In those circumstances, the VA can provide the dental treatment necessary to establish and maintain a functioning set of teeth.

Class III applies when a VA dental provider determines that a dental problem is directly aggravating another service-connected health condition. The dental treatment is aimed at addressing that connection.

Veterans participating in the Veteran Readiness and Employment program can potentially qualify under Class V when dental treatment is necessary to help them enter, continue or complete their employment rehabilitation goals.

There are also provisions for veterans whose dental problems are complicating treatment for another health condition, as well as certain veterans receiving inpatient or domiciliary care.

Another important group is recently discharged veterans. Someone who served at least 90 days on active duty during the Persian Gulf War era may qualify for one-time dental care if they meet the VA's other conditions, including applying within 180 days of discharge.

The VA also provides a one-time course of dental care for certain recently separated combat veterans, including qualifying OEF/OIF/OND veterans, subject to the applicable requirements and deadlines.

What if a veteran does not qualify for free dental care?

Not qualifying for VA dental treatment does not necessarily mean a veteran has to pay the full private-market price for dental insurance.

The VA Dental Insurance Program (VADIP) allows veterans enrolled in VA healthcare to purchase private dental insurance at reduced rates. CHAMPVA beneficiaries can also qualify. Current VADIP plans are offered through Delta Dental and MetLife.

VADIP plans can include preventive and diagnostic treatment, restorative and endodontic services, oral surgery and emergency dental care.

However, the veteran pays the insurance premium and any applicable copayments, so it is different from receiving dental treatment directly through the VA .

Importantly, signing up for VADIP does not remove a veteran's eligibility for free VA dental services if they qualify for them.

Veterans who have not yet enrolled in VA healthcare generally need to do so before seeking VA dental treatment. The VA says eligible veterans can apply using the 10-10EZ health care application, while those already enrolled do not need to reapply.

With VA reporting that nearly 888,000 veterans received dental care in fiscal year 2025, the program remains an important benefit, but eligibility depends heavily on the individual's circumstances rather than veteran status alone.

For the most accurate answer, veterans should check their specific VA dental eligibility class before assuming a procedure will be covered or free.

articles.title: How much will your monthly payment grow with the latest 2027 COLA forecast?
articles.standfirst: Social Security beneficiaries could see a noticeably larger increase in 2027, but the final figure is still months away
articles.summary: Social Security beneficiaries could see a noticeably larger increase in 2027, but the final figure is still months away
articles.body:
S ocial Security recipients are looking at another increase in their monthly benefits next year, although the size of the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) remains uncertain.

The latest forecast from AARP puts the potential 2027 COLA at 3.5%, based on the inflation data available so far. That estimate is not the official adjustment, however, and it could move higher or lower as additional inflation figures are released.

For comparison, Social Security benefits received a 2.8% COLA in 2026. The latest projection would therefore represent a larger increase for beneficiaries if it ultimately becomes the official figure.

So, what could that mean for your monthly check?

The answer depends on the size of your current benefit. A 3.5% increase would add approximately $35 for every $1,000 in monthly benefits. Someone currently receiving $1,500 a month, for example, would see an increase of about $52.50, bringing the benefit to approximately $1,552.50.

A recipient collecting $2,000 would gain about $70 per month, while someone receiving $2,500 would see an increase of roughly $87.50.

The Social Security Administration reported that the average monthly benefit for retired workers was $2,084.40 in June 2026. If that amount were simply increased by 3.5%, the monthly payment would rise by approximately $72.95, producing a new benefit of around $2,157.35.

Those figures are illustrations rather than guarantees because individual benefits differ substantially.

Why the 2027 Social Security increase can still change

The most important point for beneficiaries is that the 3.5% figure is still a forecast.

Social Security's COLA is tied to the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W).

The government does not simply use the latest annual inflation number. Instead, the calculation uses the average CPI-W readings for July, August and September and compares that third-quarter average with the applicable comparison period from the previous year.

That means the July figure is only the beginning of the final calculation. August and September inflation data can still change the outlook.

Recent forecasts have already demonstrated how quickly expectations can move. Earlier projections were higher before inflation cooled, with the latest estimates generally falling into the mid-3% range.

One recent estimate from the Senior Citizens League put the potential increase at 3.6%, slightly above AARP's 3.5% projection.

The distinction of a tenth of a percentage point may sound insignificant, but it becomes more noticeable over a full year and for people receiving larger benefits.

For example, on a $2,084.40 monthly benefit, a 3.5% increase would mean roughly $73 more each month. A 3.6% increase would produce about $75 more. Over 12 months, that difference would amount to roughly $25.

The official COLA will not be known until the Social Security Administration has the necessary third-quarter inflation data.

The increase would then apply to benefits beginning in January 2027. The SSA explains that COLAs are designed to prevent inflation from eroding the purchasing power of Social Security and SSI benefits.

A bigger check does not necessarily mean more spending power

While an increase in benefits is welcome news, retirees should not assume the entire COLA will translate into extra money available for everyday expenses.

Medicare premiums are one factor that can affect the amount beneficiaries actually receive. If Medicare costs rise, some of the Social Security increase can effectively be absorbed by higher deductions.

There is also a broader question about whether the CPI-W accurately reflects the expenses faced by older Americans.

Healthcare, housing and other costs can have a particularly significant impact on retirees, meaning an increase based on overall inflation does not necessarily match every beneficiary's personal experience.

For now, however, the best available estimate is that Social Security recipients could receive a 3.5% increase in 2027, with other forecasts placing the figure slightly higher.

The number remains provisional, and the next rounds of inflation data will determine whether beneficiaries ultimately receive more or less.

For someone receiving around the current average retired-worker benefit of $2,084.40, a 3.5% COLA would mean approximately $73 more per month, or about $875 more over a full year, before considering any changes to Medicare deductions or other factors.

The final number will come into focus once the September inflation figures are available, making the next few months particularly important for anyone planning their 2027 retirement budget.

articles.title: Who is Natalie Harp? Donald Trump's right-hand woman embroiled in scandal involving secret letters to the President
articles.standfirst: The little-known Trump aide has become a major political talking point after revelations about her extraordinary loyalty and private correspondence with the president
articles.summary: The little-known Trump aide has become a major political talking point after revelations about her extraordinary loyalty and private correspondence with the president
articles.body:
Natalie Harp has spent years operating largely behind the scenes in US President Donald Trump 's political world.

Now, the 35-year-old White House aide has suddenly become one of the most discussed figures surrounding the president after reports revealed the existence of intensely personal letters she wrote to Trump .

Harp's unusual closeness to the president has already attracted attention inside and outside the White House.

Her role has also come under renewed scrutiny following comments from Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff and reports about her involvement in Trump's communications and inner circle.

The latest controversy centers on private letters written by Harp to Trump in 2023.

The correspondence, obtained by The Daily Beast and subsequently reported on by other outlets, has raised questions about the nature of Harp's relationship with the president and the extent of her influence.

In one letter, Harp reportedly wrote: “I never want to bring you anything but joy. I'm sorry I lost my focus. You are all that matters to me. I don't want to ever let you down. Thank you for being my guardian and protector in this life.”

The letter was signed, “with all my heart, Natalie.” Another included a similarly emotional passage in which Harp asked Trump to tell her when she made mistakes and said he had the right to reprimand her.

The revelations have intensified interest in an aide who was already known for being exceptionally loyal to Trump .

How Natalie Harp rose into Trump's inner circle

Harp's connection with Trump dates back to her experience as a cancer survivor.

She has publicly credited Trump 's first-term Right to Try legislation with helping her access treatment, although medical experts have disputed whether the law was actually necessary for her to receive the drug she was given.

That experience helped propel Harp into the conservative political spotlight. She spoke at the 2020 Republican National Convention and subsequently worked as a presenter for the right-wing One America News Network.

She joined Trump 's political operation in 2022 and became a familiar presence around him during the period between his two presidencies.

By the 2024 campaign, she had earned the nickname “human printer” because she frequently carried a portable printer and supplied Trump with printed copies of news reports, social media posts and other information.

That role has continued into Trump 's second administration. Her official position is executive assistant to the president, but reporting indicates that her responsibilities extend well beyond traditional administrative duties.

She is frequently near Trump during meetings, travels and public events, and she has helped with his Truth Social posts. One episode described by CNN illustrates just how determined Harp has been to remain close to Trump.

In October 2023, when there reportedly was no room for her in Trump 's motorcade for a New York court appearance, she became involved in a confrontation with staffers before ultimately climbing into the trunk of an SUV to make the trip.

Her proximity to Trump has also reportedly frustrated some other advisers, particularly when they have wanted private meetings with the president.

At the same time, White House officials have defended her, with spokesman Davis Ingle describing Harp as “one of the most loyal and hardest working aides on President Trump’s team.”

The scrutiny intensified further after Ossoff publicly highlighted Harp 's presence around Trump , including her involvement in a secret plane switch during a trip to Turkey amid a reported security threat.

The White House strongly objected to Ossoff 's comments, while Harp 's supporters argued that the senator was unfairly targeting an aide who has simply been dedicated to her job. Nevertheless, the letters have added a new dimension to the controversy.

Critics are questioning whether Harp 's extraordinary personal loyalty could affect the information and advice reaching the president, while Trump's allies continue to portray her as a hardworking and trusted member of his team.

For now, Harp remains firmly embedded in Trump's orbit. The controversy may have made her far more recognizable to the public, but there is little indication that the attention has weakened her standing with the president.

articles.title: Trump and Melania take ‘Lap of Honor’ in The Beast before Freedom 250 Grand Prix
articles.standfirst: The ceremonial lap has become one of the signature images of the event
articles.summary: The ceremonial lap has become one of the signature images of the event
articles.body:
The inaugural Freedom 250 Grand Prix in Washington, D.C., delivered plenty of racing excitement before the green flag ever waved.

Ahead of Sunday's historic IndyCar event, President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump took a ceremonial "lap of honor" around the downtown street circuit in the presidential limousine known as "The Beast," drawing cheers from spectators gathered around the nation's capital. The ride served as one of the marquee pre-race moments before drivers took to the track for the 250-mile event.

Trump had previewed the moment before taking to the track, joking that his lap would be considerably slower than the speeds fans would later witness from IndyCar's stars.

That did little to diminish the spectacle

Riding in The Beast, Donald and Melania Trump completed the honorary circuit while fans lined the course. The ceremonial lap has become one of the signature images of the event and highlighted the race's connection to the nationwide celebrations surrounding America's 250th anniversary.

The event transformed the nation's capital into a high-speed racing venue, with open-wheel cars navigating a course that wound past some of America's most recognizable landmarks. Moments after Trump gave the signal to begin the race, drivers accelerated through the streets of Washington , including a stretch along Pennsylvania Avenue just blocks from the White House.

Before the engines roared to life, Trump and First Lady Melania Trump participated in one of the day's most memorable pre-race ceremonies. articles.title: SSDI Payment August 2026: Who is eligible to get their disability benefits the last week of the month?
articles.standfirst: The final Social Security payment of August is scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, but not every SSDI recipient will receive a payment that day
articles.summary: The final Social Security payment of August is scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, but not every SSDI recipient will receive a payment that day
articles.body:
Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) beneficiaries have one final opportunity to receive their regular August payment during the last week of the month, with the Social Security Administration (SSA) scheduled to send another batch of benefits on Wednesday, August 26.

The payment date is particularly important for beneficiaries whose birthdays fall toward the end of the month.

Under the SSA's standard payment system, eligible Social Security recipients who began receiving benefits after April 30, 1997, are assigned a Wednesday payment date based on their date of birth.

That means the August 26 payment is intended for SSDI recipients whose birthdays fall between the 21st and 31st of the month.

The date is the fourth Wednesday of August and represents the final regular Social Security payment date on the calendar for the month. Beneficiaries whose birthdays fall earlier in the month should already have received their August payments.

Those born from the 1st through the 10th were scheduled for August 12, while those born from the 11th through the 20th were scheduled for August 19.

The same birth-date system generally applies to retirement, survivor and disability benefits, although there are important exceptions.

Who qualifies for the August 26 SSDI payment?

For most people who started receiving Social Security after April 30, 1997, the payment schedule works as follows:

- Birthday from the 1st-10th: Second Wednesday of the month

- Birthday from the 11th-20th: Third Wednesday of the month

- Birthday from the 21st-31st: Fourth Wednesday of the month

Therefore, an SSDI beneficiary with a birthday on August 24, for example, would generally fall into the fourth-Wednesday group and should expect the August payment on August 26.

However, the beneficiary's own birthday is not always the date used. If someone receives benefits based on another person's earnings record, the SSA says the payment schedule is determined by the birthday of the person whose record establishes entitlement.

There are also beneficiaries who do not follow the Wednesday schedule. People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 generally receive their Social Security payment on the third day of the month.

The same third-of-the-month rule can apply to certain people who receive both Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) .

August has another calendar quirk this year. SSI is normally paid on the first day of the month, but August 1, 2026, fell on a Saturday.

As a result, the August SSI payment was moved forward to Friday, July 31. That means there is no separate SSI payment dated for August in the final week of this month.

What should you do if your SSDI payment is late?

The SSA advises beneficiaries to check their expected payment date before assuming there is a problem. The agency's official schedule confirms that payments are distributed according to benefit type and, for most post-April-1997 beneficiaries, birth date.

If the payment does not arrive as expected, beneficiaries should first check with their financial institution. The SSA also provides the my Social Security online account, which allows recipients to view information about their benefits and payment schedule.

The SSA's 2026 payment calendar notes that if a payment does not arrive on the expected date, beneficiaries should allow additional time before contacting the agency.

For SSDI recipients born between the 21st and 31st, then, Wednesday, August 26 is the key date to watch. It is the final scheduled Wednesday payment of August, although individual circumstances can change which payment cycle applies.

The next Social Security payment cycle will begin in September, so understanding which schedule applies can help beneficiaries plan bills, housing costs and other monthly expenses without mistaking the staggered payment system for a missed benefit.

articles.title: Costco Tariff Refund: Are you getting a payment from the wholesale store soon? This is what we know
articles.standfirst: Costco has said members will benefit if the retailer recovers tariff payments, but shoppers should not expect a direct check to arrive automatically
articles.summary: Costco has said members will benefit if the retailer recovers tariff payments, but shoppers should not expect a direct check to arrive automatically
articles.body:
C ostco shoppers hoping for a tariff refund may need to adjust their expectations.

Although the wholesale giant has repeatedly said it intends to return value to members if it recovers money from the federal government, there is currently no announced program sending individual Costco customers direct cash payments.

The issue stems from tariffs imposed under the Trump administration that were later struck down by the Supreme Court.

Businesses that paid the affected tariffs are pursuing refunds from the government, potentially creating a huge pool of money that retailers could recover.

Consumers, however, generally were not the importers of record and therefore cannot simply apply to the government for the money themselves. That distinction is crucial for Costco members.

Costco CEO Ron Vachris previously said the company would seek to return the value of any recovered tariff charges to its members.

He has emphasized that the retailer would do so through lower prices and better value rather than necessarily sending checks to individual shoppers.

That promise has become increasingly significant as major retailers begin reporting billions of dollars in tariff refunds.

What Costco has promised its members

Costco's position is somewhat different from the idea of a conventional consumer refund.

In March, Vachris said: “When legal challenges have recovered charges passed on in some form to our members, our commitment will be to find the best way to return this value to our members through lower prices and better values.”

The company has also stressed that it did not necessarily pass the entire cost of tariffs on to shoppers.

Costco used several strategies to limit the effect on prices, including changing sourcing locations, consolidating purchases and relying more heavily on its Kirkland Signature private-label products.

That makes calculating an individual customer's supposed refund particularly difficult.

A shopper who spent hundreds or thousands of dollars at Costco during the tariff period cannot simply calculate a percentage of those purchases and expect that amount back. The impact of tariffs varied depending on the product, supplier, country of origin and timing.

The uncertainty has nevertheless resulted in legal action. A proposed class-action lawsuit filed against Costco argues that customers who paid higher prices should receive compensation if the company subsequently recovers the tariff money from the government.

The lawsuit contends that reducing prices for future shoppers would not necessarily compensate people who already paid more.

Will Costco send members checks?

There is currently no indication that Costco is preparing a universal direct-payment program for members.

Instead, the company's public position has centered on returning the benefit through pricing and other forms of value. That could mean lower prices on selected merchandise rather than a one-time payment tied to an individual's previous purchases.

The broader retail landscape makes the distinction even more important. Forbes reported on August 21 that America's largest retailers had reported receiving more than $5 billion in tariff refunds during the week alone, but many companies were not directly passing those payments back to the consumers who originally absorbed some of the tariff costs.

Walmart, for example, has said it intends to use its multibillion-dollar refund to help reduce prices, while Target also received a substantial reimbursement.

These approaches show that retailers have considerable discretion over how they translate government refunds into consumer benefits.

For Costco members, therefore, the most accurate answer is that a tariff-related benefit may eventually reach shoppers, but a direct Costco check is not currently something customers should count on.

The legal cases surrounding the refunds could also affect what happens next. Costco has faced pressure from customers who argue that people who paid higher prices during the tariff period should receive compensation rather than simply benefiting from lower prices in the future.

Until the refund process is finalized and Costco announces a specific mechanism, shoppers should be wary of websites or social-media posts claiming that members need to submit personal information to claim an immediate “Costco tariff refund.”

For now, the company's promise is centered on “lower prices and better values”, not an automatic cash payment. If Costco ultimately receives substantial tariff reimbursements, members could see the benefit at the checkout rather than in their bank accounts.

articles.summary: Tonight's Powerball drawing offers an estimated $81 million jackpot, with the winning numbers to be announced after the draw
articles.body:
P owerball players are waiting for the winning numbers from the Monday, August 24, 2026, drawing, with an estimated $81 million jackpot up for grabs.

At the time of writing, the August 24 drawing has not yet taken place, meaning the official winning numbers are not available yet.

The drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, so anyone looking for the numbers ahead of the drawing will need to wait until the official draw has been completed. Powerball's official website confirms that drawings take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday at 10:59 p.m. ET.

The estimated $81 million prize follows Saturday night's drawing, which failed to produce a jackpot winner. The numbers drawn on Saturday, August 22, were 13, 31, 54, 57 and 65, with Powerball 23. The Power Play multiplier was 3X.

Because nobody matched all five white balls and the Powerball , the jackpot rolled over to Monday's drawing.

Powerball winning numbers for August 24 are still pending

Once Monday night's drawing is complete, the official results will consist of five white-ball numbers plus one red Powerball number.

Players should be careful about numbers circulating online before the drawing. The official Powerball results are the definitive source, and lottery tickets should be checked against the official numbers after the draw rather than relying solely on social-media posts or unofficial lottery websites.

The estimated jackpot for Monday is $81 million, while the estimated lump-sum cash option is approximately $34.8 million before taxes. State lottery information confirms those figures for the August 24 drawing.

Powerball tickets cost $2 per play. Players select five numbers from the white-ball pool and one Powerball number, although the lottery also offers a Quick Pick option for randomly generated selections. The game provides several ways to win prizes even without matching all six numbers.

A ticket matching all five white balls but missing the Powerball is worth $1 million under the standard prize structure. Matching fewer numbers can also produce prizes, with the Powerball alone being enough to win a smaller prize.

The Power Play option can increase eligible non-jackpot prizes for an additional $1 per play. The multiplier varies from drawing to drawing.

For Monday's drawing, the previous 3X Power Play was attached to Saturday's game, so players should check the multiplier associated with their own August 24 ticket.

What time is the Powerball drawing?

The Powerball drawing takes place at 10:59 p.m. ET on Monday, August 24. Sales deadlines are determined by individual participating jurisdictions and generally occur before the drawing. Powerball says cutoff times can vary by state and jurisdiction, so players should check their local lottery's rules.

Powerball is played across 45 states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The lottery also expanded ticket sales into the United Kingdom beginning July 21, 2026.

The jackpot can be claimed in either annuity or cash form. The advertised $81 million figure represents the estimated annuitized prize, while the cash option is considerably smaller because it represents the amount available as a one-time payment before applicable taxes.

For now, however, there is no August 24 winning combination to report. The winning numbers are pending until tonight's 10:59 p.m. ET drawing.

articles.title: Scientists on alert after discovering rapid movement of dangerous US fault line could soon trigger major earthquake
articles.standfirst: The potentially significant discovery could help experts refine estimates of how often major earthquakes strike
articles.summary: The potentially significant discovery could help experts refine estimates of how often major earthquakes strike
articles.body:
A quiet stretch of the San Andreas Fault in Northern California is giving scientists a potentially important new reason to reconsider how quickly one of the nation’s most dangerous fault systems is moving.

Researchers at San Jose State University have uncovered geological evidence suggesting the Santa Cruz Mountains section of the fault has maintained a faster, more consistent slip rate than previously estimated.

The work, which hasn't yet been formally published, is based on signs preserved in the landscape around Sanborn County Park and appears to trace the fault’s movement across roughly 10,000 years.

That long-term picture matters. Faults that slip more rapidly can generally accumulate and release strain more frequently, potentially affecting estimates of how often damaging earthquakes may occur.

The finding doesn't mean a major earthquake is imminent, and scientists still cannot predict exactly when or where the next large rupture will happen.

It does, however, provide another clue about how the San Andreas behaves over thousands of years rather than just within the relatively short period covered by modern monitoring.

Why a faster slip rate could matter

The San Andreas Fault stretches for nearly 800 miles through California, marking the boundary where the Pacific Plate moves past the North American Plate .

Its destructive history includes the 1857 Fort Tejon earthquake and the 1906 San Francisco earthquake, two events that helped cement the fault’s reputation as one of the most consequential seismic threats in the United States.

Scientists have spent decades trying to determine how quickly different segments move, how much strain they accumulate and how those factors influence future earthquakes.

The latest San Jose State research suggests the Santa Cruz Mountains segment may not have slowed over time as previously assumed. Instead, its movement appears to have remained relatively stable across approximately 10 millennia.

Separate research released earlier this year has also heightened scientific interest in California’s fault network, with studies suggesting portions of the San Andreas and nearby San Jacinto systems are experiencing unusually elevated stress.

Those findings have inevitably revived discussion of California’s feared “Big One,” although earthquake scientists consistently caution against interpreting elevated stress or faster fault movement as a countdown to a specific event.

Scientists looking beyond prediction

The real value of the new research lies in improving hazard assessment rather than forecasting a precise date.

More accurate slip-rate estimates can help scientists refine earthquake probability models, while emergency planners can use that information when evaluating building standards, transportation systems and other critical infrastructure.

That distinction is crucial because much of an earthquake’s human impact comes from what happens above the fault rather than beneath it. Buildings, bridges, roads and utilities that cannot withstand severe shaking can turn a natural event into a catastrophe.

California has strengthened construction standards and seismic planning over decades, but new discoveries can change how experts understand which areas may face the greatest long-term risk.

The San Andreas will continue moving whether people feel it or not. What scientists are trying to determine is whether that movement is occurring faster than assumed, and what that means for the millions of people living near one of the world’s best-known fault systems.

articles.title: “I’ve had enough of her”: Trump and Melania's heated argument sparks intense speculation at Freedom 250
articles.standfirst: A lip reader has offered a striking interpretation of the couple’s conversation during the IndyCar Freedom 250
articles.summary: A lip reader has offered a striking interpretation of the couple’s conversation during the IndyCar Freedom 250
articles.body:
A celebration of speed, spectacle and American history briefly gave way to a far more personal moment Sunday when First Lady Melania Trump and President Donald Trump were filmed in what appeared to be a tense conversation at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix .

The exchange quickly circulated online after IndyCar ’s first race through Washington, D.C., with a lip reader offering an interpretation of what the president and first lady may have been saying. Neither Donald Trump nor Melania Trump has confirmed the accuracy of that interpretation.

According to the lip reader cited in the report, Melania appeared to say: “That is private and valuable text.” Trump was then interpreted as asking: “Was it enough?”

“I don’t know,” Melania allegedly replied, before Trump appeared to answer: “Then I need to see it.”

The conversation seemed to become more pointed from there. “Donald, listen, I’m gonna go,” Melania appeared to say.

articles.standfirst: A brief Freedom 250 moment reignited questions about one of the president’s most closely watched aides
articles.summary: A brief Freedom 250 moment reignited questions about one of the president’s most closely watched aides
articles.body:
A few seconds of video from the Freedom 250 Grand Prix have become the latest flashpoint around President Donald Trump , First Lady Melania Trump and presidential aide Natalie Harp , after the First Lady was seen walking away moments before Harp moved back toward the president.

The clip, filmed during Sunday’s IndyCar race in Washington D.C., shows Trump seated with Melania nearby. She then stands, adjusts her skirt and leaves the immediate conversation.

Shortly afterward, Harp approaches the president, who appears to hand her a cellphone and give her a brief instruction before she steps back while remaining close.

Nothing in the footage proves there was tension between the women, but the timing was enough to fuel online speculation because of the attention already surrounding Harp ’s access to Trump .

“Wow! This video is so much more interesting when you realize that the woman who comes in right before Melania is getting up to leave is Natalie Harp ,” one critic wrote on social media.

Another person speculated: “I think she kept getting in Melania’s face to p*ssed her off!”

Why Natalie Harp’s presence is drawing so much attention

Harp has become a familiar figure at Trump ’s side during his second term after also working closely with him in Florida while he was out of office.

That visibility has generated increased scrutiny in recent weeks, particularly after reports described an unusually intense level of personal devotion to the president.

New York Times reporter Maggie Haberman said during a CNN appearance that Harp had left letters for Trump in private areas during the four years between his administrations.

“Harp has carved out this role of being incredibly devoted to the president,” Haberman said. “She had left these letters for him and in his personal spaces during the interregnum for four years.”

Haberman added: “The Secret Service had gotten alarmed by some of them.”

One reported letter allegedly included the line: “You are all that matters to me.”

An unnamed source cited by Semafor also claimed Melania Trump disliked the media attention surrounding her husband’s professional relationship with Harp , saying: “The First Lady doesn’t like these types of things.”

Freedom 250 video adds to existing speculation

The conversation around Harp has also been fueled by accounts of how closely she stays to the president.

Her estranged brother, Preston Harp , has described her focus on Trump as an “obsession,” while other reports have detailed instances in which she allegedly went to unusual lengths to remain near him.

Former Republican strategist and prominent Trump critic Rick Wilson has similarly argued that Harp ’s role is built around unwavering loyalty.

“She’s earned her place in the Trump pantheon by being the absolute unconditional ‘Yes, I love you, Mr. President,’” Wilson said.

Sunday’s video doesn't confirm any rivalry between Melania and Harp , nor does it reveal why the first lady walked away when she did.

What it does show is another ordinary-looking interaction transformed into a major talking point because of the scrutiny already surrounding Harp ’s place in Trump’s inner circle.
